record.paper_title: Open problems in the Kontsevich graph construction of Poisson bracket symmetries
record.original_question: Is there a universal extension of the Kontsevich construction from affine Poisson manifolds to the commutative but non-associative calculus of cyclic words with pair-of-pants multiplication in formal noncommutative or super-geometry, such that it remains well defined for the full family of graph-encoded symmetries Q∈sym([[P,P]]=0) of Poisson structures?

evidence.quote: Problem 20. Is there a well-defined – and universal w.r.t. the set Q ∈ sym([[P,P]] = 0) of graph-encoded symmetries of Poisson structures P – generalisation of the Kontsevich construction, originally on affine Poisson manifolds (M^r<∞_aff,P), to the commutative non-associative calculus of cyclic words with their topological pair-of-pants multiplication S^1 × S^1 → S^1 in the Kontsevich formal noncommutative (super)geometry ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. Let $(M^r_{\mathrm{aff}}, P)$ denote a finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifold, where $P = \tfrac{1}{2} P^{ij}(x)\,\partial_i \wedge \partial_j$ is a Poisson bivector, i.e. a bivector satisfying the Jacobi identity $[\![P,P]\!] = 0$ in the Schouten algebra of polyvector fields. Kontsevich's graph construction associates, to every suitable directed graph $\Gamma$ on $n$ aerial vertices and to a Poisson bivector $P$, a polydifferential operator $\Gamma(P)$ built by placing a copy of $P$ at each aerial vertex and contracting derivations along the edges; this construction yields, in particular, the graph cocycles producing infinitesimal symmetries (flows) $\dot P = Q(P)$ of the Maurer–Cartan equation $[\![P,P]\!]=0$. Denote by 
\[
\mathrm{sym}\bigl([\![P,P]\!]=0\bigr) := \bigl\{ Q \;:\; [\![P,Q(P)]\!] = 0 \text{ for every Poisson } P \bigr\}
\]
the set of all such graph-encoded symmetries.

On the other hand, Kontsevich's formal noncommutative (super)geometry replaces the commutative algebra of functions by the commutative but non-associative calculus of cyclic words, equipped with the topological pair-of-pants multiplication 
\[
\mu : S^1 \times S^1 \longrightarrow S^1,
\]
which, on cyclic words in noncommuting (super)variables, defines a commutative non-associative product compatible with the cyclic structure. In this framework, polyvector fields and Schouten-type brackets admit cyclic-word analogues.

Question. Does there exist a generalisation $\widetilde{\Gamma}$ of the Kontsevich graph construction from affine Poisson manifolds $(M^r_{\mathrm{aff}}, P)$ to the commutative non-associative calculus of cyclic words with pair-of-pants multiplication, such that $\widetilde{\Gamma}$ is:

(i) well defined as an operation on cyclic words (respecting cyclic invariance and the pair-of-pants product), and

(ii) universal with respect to the full family of graph-encoded symmetries $Q \in \mathrm{sym}([\![P,P]\!]=0)$ of Poisson structures, in the sense that for every such $Q$ the noncommutative lift $\widetilde{Q}$ is simultaneously well defined and yields a symmetry of the cyclic-word analogue of the Maurer–Cartan equation?

Construct such a universal extension or prove that no such extension exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in the list of open problems on the Kontsevich graph construction of Poisson bracket symmetries. No publication has been located that constructs such a universal noncommutative extension or rules it out, so the problem appears to remain open.
